Original Requirements: Develop a Center-to-Center (C2C) Communications Network for TxDOT to connect Traffic Management Centers (TMCs). The system must implement a repository for traffic data and exchange device control information using ITS standards (TMDD, DATEX/ASN, TCP/IP). It requires interfaces for various devices (DMS, CCTV, Ramp Meters, Signals, etc.), a Web Map application for visualization, Incident GUI for data entry, and Remote Center Control GUI for device management. The system must be configurable, scalable (local to statewide), and operate in Normal and Test modes on a Windows NT environment.
Product Goals: Establish standardized interoperability between dissimilar traffic management systems using ITS TMDD standards
Enable real-time traffic data exchange and secure remote device control across regional and statewide networks
Ensure system configurability and scalability to support future ITS application extensions and agency deployments
User Stories: As a Traffic Operator, I want to view real-time traffic conditions and incidents on a web map so I can respond quickly to congestion.
As a Center Manager, I want to remotely control Dynamic Message Signs and Lane Signals so I can manage traffic flow during emergencies.
As a System Administrator, I want to configure software building blocks for different agencies so the system can be deployed across multiple centers easily.
As a Data Analyst, I want to access standardized traffic data via the TMDD repository so I can perform regional traffic analysis.
As a Security Officer, I want to enforce username and password authentication for all device control commands so unauthorized access is prevented.
Competitive Analysis: Legacy TMC Systems: Siloed data architectures, lack standardized exchange protocols, high integration cost.
Proprietary ITS Solutions: Vendor lock-in risks, expensive licensing, limited flexibility for multi-agency use.
Open-source ITS Platforms: Community support available, but may lack specific TxDOT TMDD compliance out-of-the-box.
Cloud-based Traffic Management: Modern scalability, but potential challenges integrating with legacy hardware interfaces.
Regional Data Hubs: Effective locally, but often lack the statewide scalability defined in C2C requirements.
Direct Point-to-Point Links: Simple to implement initially, but difficult to scale and maintain standards compliance.
National ITS Architecture Compliant Systems: High standardization, but implementation quality and cost vary significantly.

Requirement Analysis: The project requires a robust backend capable of handling TMDD/DATEX/ASN messaging over TCP/IP. Key functional areas include Data Collection (storage of TMDD elements), Device Control (secure commands for DMS, CCTV, Signals, etc.), and Visualization (Web Map via ARC IMS). The architecture relies on configurable building blocks to support multi-agency deployment. Security is critical, requiring authentication for all control commands. The specified technology stack (Windows NT, C/C++, ARC IMS) is legacy, posing maintenance and compatibility risks that should be addressed in modernization planning. The system must support both Normal (operational) and Test (logging) modes.
Requirement Pool: Implement TMDD standard compliance including message sets for data transmission using DATEX/ASN over TCP/IP
Develop secure remote device control interfaces for DMS, CCTV, LCS, and Signals with username/password authentication
Create Web Map application using ARC IMS to display traffic conditions, incidents, and device statuses
Design configurable software building blocks to allow deployment across different agencies and configurations
Implement Normal and Test operation modes with activity logging for system diagnostics
UI Design draft: The UI consists of three main components: 1) Web Map Interface: Displays interstates/highways with color-coded links for speed, incident icons, and device statuses (DMS, CCTV). Supports zoom and pan. 2) Incident GUI: Forms for entering/modifying incident and lane closure data, plus lists for managing existing records. 3) Remote Control GUI: Login screen, device selection lists (networks, DMS, CCTV, etc.), command input fields (messages, plans), and scrollable status logs. Style should be functional, high-contrast for control rooms, using ESRI Map Objects for mapping components.
Anything UNCLEAR: The SRS specifies 'Microsoft Windows NT' and 'ESRI ARC IMS', which are obsolete technologies. Clarification is needed on whether modern OS (Windows Server/Linux) and modern GIS frameworks (ArcGIS Enterprise/Web AppBuilder) are permissible replacements. The term 'Cloud' is used metaphorically for the repository network; clarification is needed on whether actual cloud infrastructure (AWS/Azure) is intended for deployment or if it remains on-premise. Specific security protocols beyond username/password (e.g., encryption, OAuth) are not detailed.
